To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the structures of ammonium salts of three different carboxylic acid anions, namely 3,5-di-nitrobenzene, 4-ni-trobenzene and 2, 4-dichloro-benzene, have been determined.

ammonium 3.5-dinitro- benzoate, ammonium 4- nitrobenzoate and ammonium 24-dichlorobenzene form hydrogen-bonding networks in which primary cation- anion interactions are through conjoined R4.3.10 and R4.2.8 motifs, with the latter being centrosymmetric.

the hydrogen-bonded three-dimensional structure of ammonium 2-chloro-5-nitrobenzene-1-carboxylate is not consistent with a previously indicated trend, and that the structures of ammonium salts of benzoic acids with two nitro substituents, one nitro substituent and one chloro substituent or two chloro substituents are all two-dimensional, with the layers lying parallel to the (001), (100) and (001)
In summary, our research is concerned with
the structures of hydrogen-bonded salts of carboxylate groups and, in particular, the role of the carboxylate O atom that is not involved in hydrogen bonding.
the hydrogen-bonded structure of salts of ionic liquids, viz. ammonium salts of organic carboxylic and nitro acids, and with the influence on the structure of the cation, anion and solvent molecules.
hydrogen-bonded supramolecular structures in salts of aromatic carboxylic and dicarboxylic acids.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the hydrogen-bonded structure adopted by an ammonium salt of a carboxylic acid depends on the nature of both the cation and anion.

the ammonium salts, (I), (II) and/or (III), of 3, 4 and 2, 4-substituted benzoates, respectively, form hydrogen-bonding polymeric structures, but the nature of these structures is dependent on the substituents and the presence or absence of water.

, in the absence of specific structural constraints, ammonium salts of monocarboxylic acids form two-dimensional hydrogen-bonded arrays, and the anions are O-carboxylates, but the anions may be either O,O'- or O-carboxylated, and the cation-anion association may be cyclic or linear.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

ammonium salts of aromatic carboxylic acid anions with O,O'-car-boxylates form three-dimensional structures through conjoined hydrogen bonds, while those with O-carboxylates form two-dimensional structures.

, with the ammonium salts, hydrogen-bonded three-dimensional polymeric networks are favoured over two-dimensional ones, and that the hydrogen bonding in the carboxylate groups plays an important role in determining the structures.

the structures of ammonium salts of monocarboxylic acids with the formula NH4(+)(RCO2(-))nH2O (n = 0-2) are dominated by the presence of O,O'-car-boxylate groups in their hydrogen-bonding schemes, but this is not true for salts with the formula NH3(+) · RC(OH)(COO(-)) · H2O.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the hydrogen-bonded three-dimensional polymeric structure of (I), with the O-carboxylates as hydrogen-bond acceptors, is the most thermodynamically favourable among the three salts.
hydrogen-bonding interactions in these salts are complex and subtle.
the hydrogen bonding in these three salts is dominated by carboxylate O atoms, with nitro O atoms playing only a minor role.
